mainTopic: Which half-sisters count as a legal sister, and how a child's status follows a שפחה or גויה mother
overview: The גמרא reads בת אשת אביך (the daughter of your father's wife) to mean that a half-sister counts only if her mother could have a marriage bond with the father. It then tests how far that limit goes. רב פפא shows that קידושין take effect with חייבי לאוין, so a sister from such a mother counts. רבא uses 'born at home or born outside' to include even a sister from a כרת union. A sister from a שפחה or a גויה stays excluded, because no marriage with them is possible, and a woman who converts is treated as a new person. The גמרא then asks where the רבנן learn these exclusions. For a שפחה they use 'the wife and her children shall be her master's.' For a גויה they use 'כי יסיר את בנך', which teaches that a child from a גויה is her son, not his father's. רבינא learns from the same פסוק that a daughter's son from a גוי is still 'your son'. The גמרא explains that this makes him Jewish and not a ממזר, but still a ישראל פסול. Finally, the פסוק covers every nation, not just the seven nations, because the opinion that argues with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is רבי שמעון, who learns from the reason a פסוק gives.

steps.title: Maybe the phrase leaves out a sister from a forbidden union
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that בת אשת אביך might also leave out a sister whose mother was forbidden to the father by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the phrase comes to exclude women who are forbidden by a negative commandment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If בת אשת אביך means the mother must be a proper wife, maybe a woman forbidden to the father by a לאו doesn't count either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading excluded a שפחה and a גויה because the father cannot marry them. The challenge asks whether a woman the father is forbidden to marry, such as a ממזרת, is also not a real 'wife'. If so, her daughter would not count as his sister.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (introduces a suggested alternative reading)
Women forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)

phrases.english: But say: it comes to exclude those forbidden by negative commandments!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the phrase בת אשת אביך from ויקרא 18:11, which the גמרא was just explaining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the earlier reading of בת אשת אביך reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that בת אשת אביך requires a real marriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'wife' means a proper wife, a forbidden wife might not qualify either

steps.title: רב פפא: marriage takes effect even with a forbidden woman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that קידושין take effect with חייבי לאוין, so such a woman is still really 'your father's wife'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: with women forbidden by negative commandments, betrothal takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. A woman forbidden by a לאו is still legally married once the קידושין are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is not whether the marriage was allowed. The test is whether a marriage bond exists. With חייבי לאוין the marriage is forbidden but still valid, so her daughter is בת אשת אביך.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the act that creates a marriage bond

steps.confusionAlert: Forbidden does not mean invalid. With a לאו the marriage should not happen, but if it does happen, it really counts.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
with those forbidden by negative commandments, betrothal takes effect,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין תָּפְשִׂי בְּהוּ קִדּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the legal status of the case so it fits the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forbidden wife is not a real wife
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין take effect with חייבי לאוין, so she is truly אשת אביך

steps.title: Proof from the beloved and hated wives
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a man with two wives, one 'beloved' and one 'hated', shows that even a forbidden marriage is still called a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'If a man has two wives, one beloved and one hated.' Is anyone beloved or hated before God? Rather, 'beloved' means her marriage is beloved (permitted), and 'hated' means her marriage is hated (forbidden). And the Torah still says 'If [a man] has', meaning both are his wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב פפא's rule. The 'hated' wife is one whose marriage was forbidden, yet the Torah calls her his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rejects the idea that God loves one woman and hates another. So 'hated' must describe a forbidden marriage. Since the פסוק still says the man 'has' her as a wife, forbidden marriages do take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: as it is written: "If a man has two wives,
the one beloved and the other hated";
but is there one beloved before God
and one hated before God?
Rather, "beloved" means beloved in her marriage,
phrases.notes: Her marriage was a permitted one.

phrases.english: "hated" means hated in her marriage,
phrases.notes: Her marriage was a forbidden one.

phrases.english: and the Torah says: "If [a man] has [them]."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים הָאַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְהָאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב פפא's rule
steps.raayaObject: קידושין take effect with חייבי לאוין
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 21:15: the 'hated' wife is still called his wife
steps.whatToRemember: With חייבי לאוין, קידושין take effect. A sister from such a mother is fully his sister.

steps.title: Maybe it leaves out a sister from a כרת union
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests that בת אשת אביך leaves out a sister whose mother was forbidden to the father by כרת, where קידושין do not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it comes to exclude women forbidden under the penalty of כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a stronger challenge. With חייבי כריתות there is no marriage at all, so maybe her daughter is not his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer worked because קידושין take effect with a לאו. With כרת they do not take effect. So the earlier logic seems to exclude this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden under the penalty of כרת, where קידושין do not take effect

phrases.english: But say: it comes to exclude those liable to karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates the challenge from לאוין to כריתות, where step 2's answer no longer works
steps.kashyaTarget: Including a sister born from a union the father was forbidden to under כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without valid קידושין the mother is not אשת אביך, so the daughter should be excluded

steps.title: רבא: 'born at home or born outside' includes her
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a פסוק that calls her 'your sister' whether the father may keep the mother or must send her away. This includes even a כרת union.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the verse says, 'The nakedness of your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born outside.' This means whether your father is told 'keep her' or told 'send her away', the Torah says 'she is your sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers from a different פסוק. A sister from a forbidden union, even one with no marriage at all, is still his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'born at home' as a woman the father may keep, and 'born outside' as a woman he must send away. 'Must send away' covers even חייבי כריתות. So this פסוק includes the case that בת אשת אביך seemed to leave out.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתְךָ בַת אָבִיךָ אוֹ בַת אִמֶּךָ
phrases.english: "The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother,
born at home or born outside":
whether they tell your father: keep her,
or whether they tell your father: send her away,
and the Torah says: "She is your sister."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתְךָ בַת אָבִיךָ אוֹ בַת אִמֶּךָ מוֹלֶדֶת בַּיִת אוֹ מוֹלֶדֶת חוּץ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 with a separate פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: An additional פסוק that includes the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sister from a כרת union is excluded because there are no קידושין
steps.terutzMaskana: מולדת חוץ includes even a sister from a union the father must end, such as חייבי כריתות

steps.title: Then include a sister from a maidservant or gentile too
steps.stepSummary: If 'keep her or send her away' includes forbidden unions, maybe it also includes a sister born from a שפחה or a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: whether your father says 'keep her' or 'send her away', the Torah says 'she is your sister.' That would include his sister from a maidservant or a gentile woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבא's reading around. If even a union with no marriage counts, why not a שפחה or גויה too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's פסוק seems to ignore whether a marriage exists. If so, it could cover a sister from a שפחה or גויה as well. That would undo the starting rule that excluded them.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בֵּין שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ אָבִיךָ קַיֵּים,
phrases.english: Say: whether your father says to her: stay,
or whether your father says: leave,
and the Torah says: "She is your sister",
to include his sister from a maidservant or a gentile woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בֵּין שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ אָבִיךָ קַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading by stretching it further
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's broad reading of מולדת חוץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק doesn't require a marriage, it should include a sister from a שפחה or גויה too

steps.title: A marriage bond must be possible
steps.stepSummary: בת אשת אביך still requires a woman who can have a marriage bond with the father. That leaves out a שפחה and a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'the daughter of your father's wife': a woman with whom your father can have a marriage bond. This excludes his sister from a maidservant or a gentile woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to בת אשת אביך. That phrase sets the outer limit: the father must at least be capable of marrying her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים work together. מולדת חוץ includes forbidden unions, even כרת ones. בת אשת אביך still requires a woman who could in principle marry a Jew, so a שפחה and a גויה stay excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: A marriage bond (the ability to be married)
The daughter of your father's wife

steps.whatToRemember: A sister from any Jewish mother counts, whether the mother was permitted, forbidden by a לאו, or forbidden by כרת. Only a sister from a שפחה or גויה is excluded, because there marriage is impossible.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'marriage bond' here means the category of women who can marry at all. It does not mean the case where קידושין actually took effect.

phrases.english: The verse says: "The daughter of your father's wife":

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִישׁוּת לְאָבִיךָ בָּהּ,
phrases.english: one with whom your father can have a marriage bond,
which excludes his sister from a maidservant or a gentile woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by restoring the limit set by בת אשת אביך
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק limits the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מולדת חוץ includes even a sister from a שפחה or גויה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only women capable of a marriage bond are included, so a sister from a שפחה or גויה is excluded

steps.title: Why include the כרת case and not the שפחה or גויה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we decided to include a sister from a כרת union and to leave out a sister from a שפחה or גויה, rather than the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what made you decide this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we knew which case to include and which to leave out. This sets up the next step, which gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 included the כרת case, and step 7 left out the שפחה and גויה. Both are forbidden unions, so the גמרא wants a reason for placing them on different sides.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? Meaning: what is your reason for choosing this way?

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: Why include the כרת case and leave out the שפחה and גויה, and not the other way around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why steps 5 and 7 sorted the two kinds of forbidden union differently.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for including the כרת case while excluding שפחה and גויה.

steps.title: קידושין can take effect with a woman forbidden by כרת
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to include the כרת case, because a woman forbidden by כרת can still have קידושין with other men.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason that the verse should include those forbidden by כרת, since קידושין take effect with them in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: a woman forbidden to the father by כרת is still someone who can be married in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her קידושין do not work with this father, but they do work with other men. A שפחה or גויה cannot have קידושין with any Jewish man at all. That makes the כרת woman closer to being a real 'wife'.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
Unions forbidden with the punishment of כרת
In general, with the rest of the world

phrases.english: It stands to reason
that the verse should include those liable to כרת,
since betrothal takes effect with them in general.
phrases.notes: He means with other men. She can marry someone else, even though she can't marry this father.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא חַיָּיבֵי כָּרֵיתוֹת הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כרת woman can have קידושין with other men, while a שפחה or גויה cannot have קידושין with anyone.

steps.title: A שפחה or גויה could convert and then marry him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the reverse: a שפחה or גויה should be included, since after converting she could marry this very father.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the verse should include a שפחה and a גויה, because if she converts, קידושין take effect with him himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with אדרבה. It says the שפחה or גויה has the better claim to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת woman can never marry this father, only other men. A שפחה or גויה who converts can marry this same father. So she seems closer to being 'his wife'.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the exact opposite

phrases.english: On the contrary:
it should include a maidservant and a gentile woman,
since if she converts, even with him himself
betrothal takes effect with her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה שִׁפְחָה וְגוֹיָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 9 by flipping it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of step 9, that the כרת woman is closer to marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כרת woman can marry only other men, but a converted שפחה or גויה can marry this same father, so she should count more.

steps.title: After conversion she is a new person
steps.stepSummary: A woman who converts is treated as a different body, so her later ability to marry does not help while she was a שפחה or גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she converts, she is a different body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that conversion makes her a new person. Her ability to marry after converting does not count for her status before converting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the child was born, the mother was a שפחה or גויה, and no קידושין could take effect with her. The person who can marry after conversion is treated as someone new. So the reasoning of step 9 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A different body, a new person

phrases.english: When she converts
she is a different body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the converted woman is legally a new person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שפחה or גויה should count, because she could convert and marry the father.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her future ability to marry belongs to a 'new person', so as a שפחה or גויה she has no marriage bond at all.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman forbidden by כרת still has a marriage bond with the world, so her daughter is a sister. A שפחה or גויה has no marriage bond at all, and her later conversion does not change that.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn to exclude שפחה and גויה?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the verse for a different teaching, so the גמרא asks where they learn that a sister from a שפחה or גויה is not a sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, from where do they learn to exclude a שפחה and a גויה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who do not use בת אשת אביך for this. It asks what their source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exclusion so far came from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reading of בת אשת אביך. The רבנן use that phrase for something else, so they need another source for the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
to exclude a maidservant and a gentile woman, from where do they learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן לְמַעוֹטֵי שִׁפְחָה וְגוֹיָה מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source to the source the רבנן use.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source for excluding a sister from a שפחה or גויה.

steps.title: The children follow the שפחה, not the father
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn it from the פסוק that a שפחה's children belong to her master.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from 'the wife and her children shall be her master's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the פסוק about a Hebrew slave's שפחה wife. Her children belong to the master, not to the Jewish father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the children belong to the master, they have no family tie to their Jewish father. So a daughter from a שפחה is not legally his daughter, and she is not a 'sister' to his other children.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife and her children shall be her master's

phrases.english: They derive it from 'the wife and her children'
'shall be her master's.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מֵהָאִשָּׁה וִילָדֶיהָ תִּהְיֶה לַאדוֹנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'the wife and her children shall be her master's' shows that a שפחה's children are not counted as the Jewish father's family.

steps.title: Why does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה need his own source?
steps.stepSummary: If this פסוק already teaches the rule, why does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה need בת אשת אביך for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not just use the שפחה פסוק. It looks like his source for the exclusion is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the wife and her children' already teaches the exclusion, then reading it into בת אשת אביך seems unnecessary. The גמרא needs a reason he uses both.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He means: why doesn't he just learn it from the שפחה פסוק, without needing בת אשת אביך?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 13 to question רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's separate source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's use of בת אשת אביך to exclude שפחה and גויה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'the wife and her children' already teaches the exclusion, so his source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One פסוק for the שפחה, one for the גויה
steps.stepSummary: Both sources are needed: one teaches the שפחה and the other teaches the גויה, because a גויה has family lineage and a שפחה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for a שפחה and one is for a גויה. Both are needed: if the Torah taught only the שפחה, I would say that is because she has no family lineage. But a גויה, who has family lineage, I would say is not excluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses the שפחה פסוק for the שפחה and בת אשת אביך for the גויה. It explains why we could not learn one case from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שפחה has no recognized family lineage, so it is easy to see why her child has no tie to the father. A גויה does have family lineage, so we might think her child is tied to the father. That is why a separate source is needed to exclude the גויה too.

keyTerms.meaning: One for this case, and one for that case

phrases.english: One is for a maidservant, and one is for a gentile woman.
And both are needed,
for if it had taught us only about a maidservant:
that is because she has no family lineage,
but a gentile woman, who does have family lineage,
I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources (צריכותא): each source covers a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שפחה פסוק alone covers both cases, so בת אשת אביך is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שפחה פסוק covers only the שפחה. A גויה has family lineage, so she needs her own source, בת אשת אביך.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 'the wife and her children shall be her master's' excludes the שפחה, and בת אשת אביך excludes the גויה. Two sources are needed because a גויה has family lineage and a שפחה does not.
steps.confusionAlert: The two sources are not repeating each other. Each one covers a different case, which is why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה needs both.

steps.title: Why the גויה source alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had taught only the גויה case, we could not learn the שפחה from it, because a שפחה is connected to מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had taught us only about a גויה, I would say her child is not his father's child because she has no connection to מצוות. But a שפחה does have a connection to מצוות, so I might say her child does count as the father's. That is why both sources are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the 'both are needed' answer from step 15. Now it shows why the גויה source could not teach us the שפחה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 showed that the שפחה case alone could not teach the גויה case. This step shows the other direction. A גויה is fully outside מצוות, but a שפחה keeps some מצוות. So a rule about a גויה might not carry over to a שפחה, and each case needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: She has a connection to the מצוות
I might say no (the rule would not apply)
It is needed (both sources are necessary)

steps.whatToRemember: A שפחה and a גויה each need their own source. A שפחה is connected to מצוות, and a גויה has family lineage, so neither case can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only a gentile woman —
that would be because she has no connection to the מצוות.
But a maidservant, who does have a connection to the מצוות —
I might say no. So it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכותא that began in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches a case the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the גויה source, a שפחה's child might count as the father's, since she is connected to מצוות
steps.terutzMaskana: Both פסוקים are needed for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn the rule for a גויה?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן have a source for the שפחה, but what is their source for the גויה, since one case cannot be learned from the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, we found a source for the שפחה. Where do they learn the גויה case from? And if you say we can learn it from the שפחה, we just showed that each case needs its own source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the רבנן and asks for their source for the גויה case. It also blocks the easy answer of learning it from the שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave the רבנן a source only for the שפחה. Step 16 just proved that the two cases cannot be learned from each other. So the רבנן still need a separate source for the גויה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, we found a source for a maidservant;
from where do they learn a gentile woman?
And if you say: Let us learn it from the maidservant —
these are both needed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אַשְׁכְּחַן שִׁפְחָה, גּוֹיָה מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the צריכותא just proven to show a gap in the רבנן's sources
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source that a child from a גויה is not counted as his Jewish father's child

steps.title: The source from 'כי יסיר את בנך'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, learns from the פסוק that a son from a Jewish woman is 'your son,' but a son from a גויה is called 'her son.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: The פסוק says 'for he will turn your son away from Me.' Your son from a Jewish woman is called your son. Your son from a גויה is not called your son, but her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17 by giving the רבנן a פסוק for the גויה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns against marrying non-Jews. It worries about 'your son' being led astray, meaning a child from your daughter. It does not say the same about a man's own child from a גויה, so that child is counted as hers and not his. This gives the רבנן a separate source for the גויה.

keyTerms.meaning: For he will turn your son away from Me (דברים ז:ד)

steps.whatToRemember: A child from a גויה follows the mother. He is 'her son,' not his Jewish father's son.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that Jewish status, and family relation to a Jewish father, depends on the mother.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״כִּי יָסִיר אֶת בִּנְךָ מֵאַחֲרַי״,
phrases.english: The verse says: "For he will turn your son away from Me,"
your son from a Jewish woman is called your son,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בִּנְךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹיָה קָרוּי בִּנְךָ,
phrases.english: but your son who comes from a gentile woman is not called your son,
but rather her son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כי יסיר את בנך מאחרי' shows that a son from a גויה is called her son, not his father's

steps.title: רבינא: a daughter's son from a גוי is still 'your son'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns from the same פסוק that your daughter's son from a גוי is still called your son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We can learn from this that your daughter's son from a גוי is called your son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws another lesson from the same פסוק, this time about the opposite case: a Jewish mother and a non-Jewish father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about giving your daughter to a non-Jew's son. The non-Jewish husband is the one who 'turns away', and the 'son' he turns away is the grandson born from your daughter. The פסוק still calls that grandson 'your son.' So a child from a Jewish mother and a גוי father is counted as Jewish and part of her family.

keyTerms.meaning: Who comes from a non-Jewish father

phrases.english: Ravina said: Learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בִּתְּךָ הַבָּא מִן הַגּוֹי קָרוּי בִּנְךָ.
phrases.english: your daughter's son who comes from a gentile is called your son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new lesson from the פסוק quoted in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to a Jewish woman from a גוי is called her family's child, meaning he is Jewish

steps.title: Does רבינא hold that such a child is fully כשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבינא holds that a child from a גוי or עבד with a Jewish woman is fully כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבינא holds that when a גוי or an עבד has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is כשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבינא's statement. It asks whether calling the child 'your son' means he has completely good lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether such a child is כשר is a known question. If 'your son' means fully כשר, then רבינא would be taking a clear side in it. The גמרא raises this as a possible conclusion and then checks it.

keyTerms.meaning: The child is כשר (has untainted lineage)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Ravina holds

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: that when a gentile or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman,
the child is of untainted lineage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רבינא's inference goes
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's statement that a daughter's son from a גוי is called 'your son'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is fully 'your son,' it seems the child must be completely כשר. That is a strong position to put on רבינא.

steps.title: Not a ממזר, but a ישראל פסול
steps.stepSummary: The child is not a ממזר, but he is not fully כשר either. He is called a ישראל פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he is not a ממזר. But he is not כשר either. He is called a ישראל פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 20. רבינא only meant that the child is Jewish and not a ממזר, not that his lineage is perfect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being called 'your son' shows the child is a real Jew and part of the mother's family, so he is not a ממזר. It does not show that he has full, untainted status. He can still be a ישראל פסול, with a defect in lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: A child from a forbidden union who may not marry into the Jewish people
A Jew with a defect in lineage (for example, may not marry a כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: A child from a Jewish mother and a גוי father is Jewish and not a ממזר, but according to this answer he is a ישראל פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not a ממזר' does not mean 'fully כשר.' There is a middle status, ישראל פסול, between the two.

phrases.english: Granted that he is not a mamzer —
he is also not of untainted lineage;
he is called a disqualified Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבינא holds the child is fully כשר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being called 'your son' only shows the child is Jewish and not a ממזר. It does not show untainted lineage.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבינא's child is not a ממזר, but is a ישראל פסול

steps.title: Isn't this verse only about the seven nations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source from step 18: the פסוק of 'כי יסיר' is written about the שבעה גוים, so how can it teach a rule about every גויה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this verse written about the seven nations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the source it just used. The פסוק about 'your son' comes in a section about the seven Canaanite nations, not about all גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, רבי יוחנן learned from 'כי יסיר את בנך' that a child from a גויה is 'her son,' not 'your son.' But the warning in that פסוק is about marrying the שבעה גוים. So how can it give a rule for a woman from any other nation?

keyTerms.meaning: The seven Canaanite nations living in ארץ ישראל when the Jews entered

phrases.english: Isn't this written about the seven nations?
phrases.notes: 'This' means the פסוק about not marrying them, 'כי יסיר את בנך' (דברים 7:3-4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source in step 18 and questions whether it reaches beyond the seven nations.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'כי יסיר' as a source for every גויה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's context is limited to the שבעה גוים, so it seems it cannot teach a general rule about all גוים.

steps.title: 'He will turn away' includes anyone who turns a child away
steps.stepSummary: The words 'כי יסיר' show the reason for the rule, so it includes every nation that would pull a child away from ה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For he will turn away' comes to include all those who turn away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'כי יסיר' widen the rule. Any גוי who could turn a child away from ה' is included, not just the seven nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives a reason: 'for he will turn your son away.' That reason fits every nation, not only the Canaanites. So the rule about the child being 'her son' applies to any גויה.

keyTerms.meaning: For he will turn away (part of the פסוק)
Those who turn others away (from ה')

phrases.english: "For he will turn away" —
comes to include all those who turn away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the reason stated in the פסוק as widening its scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only speaks about the שבעה גוים, so it says nothing about other nations.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק gives the reason 'כי יסיר,' it covers every גוי who could turn a child away.

steps.title: That works for רבי שמעון, but what about the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: Using the reason of a פסוק to widen it is רבי שמעון's method. The רבנן do not learn הלכה from the reason of a פסוק, so where do they get the rule about every גויה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי שמעון, who explains the reason of the verse. But for the רבנן, where do they learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer in step 23 only works for one opinion. It asks how the רבנן, who don't build on a פסוק's reason, know the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 widened the פסוק by using its reason, 'כי יסיר.' That is the method of רבי שמעון. The רבנן usually don't do this, so for them the פסוק would stay limited to the seven nations, and the גמרא asks for their source.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (for one opinion)
He learns הלכה from the reason behind the פסוק
From where do they know it?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 17. There the question was how the רבנן know about a גויה at all; here the question is only about stretching the פסוק past the seven nations.

phrases.english: This works well for רבי שמעון,
who interprets the reason of the verse,
phrases.notes: He means רבי שמעון uses the reason a מצוה is given to decide how far it reaches.

phrases.english: but for the רבנן, where do they get it from?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּדָרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 23 but shows it only fits רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן also have a source for the rule about every גויה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source from step 23 depends on learning from a פסוק's reason, which the רבנן do not do, so they seem to be left without a source.

steps.title: The opinion arguing with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'רבנן' who disagree with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה are really רבי שמעון, so his method of learning from the reason works for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who argues with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by naming who the dissenting opinion really is. The one arguing with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is רבי שמעון himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 24 assumed the opinion being discussed was the general רבנן, who don't learn from a פסוק's reason. The גמרא says no: that opinion is רבי שמעון. So the source from 'כי יסיר' works for that opinion after all, and nothing is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the teacher of this opinion)?

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'כי יסיר' covers every גויה because its reason ('he will turn away') fits every nation. This works because the opinion arguing with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is רבי שמעון, who learns from a פסוק's reason.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא who disagrees with
רבי יוסי the son of רבי יהודה —
it is רבי שמעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by naming who the dissenting opinion really is.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Naming the anonymous opinion as a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinion arguing with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the general רבנן, who would have no source for the rule about every גויה.
steps.terutzMaskana: That opinion is רבי שמעון, who learns from the reason of a פסוק, so 'כי יסיר' works as the source.
